candidate_relations.reason: Echocardiography shows normal left-ventricular wall thickness, which argues against cardiac amyloid infiltration, while the ECG specifically demonstrates advanced interatrial block and later flutter.

Dyspnea, BNP 838.6 pg/mL, left atrial enlargement, and hypertension can accompany HFpEF, but no preserved ejection fraction or diastolic assessment is provided and it does not identify the atrial conduction syndrome.
There is no smoking history, airflow obstruction, wheezing, or hyperinflation, whereas the objective abnormalities are atrial conduction delay and flutter.
